# Results — Study 752 (TGA-Drawdown)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The macro-liquidity thesis
— **a falling Treasury General Account is hidden stimulus that lifts equities over the
following weeks** — tested on a monthly **TGA operating-cash-balance** tape (a hardcoded,
clearly-labelled monthly **proxy** of the weekly FRED `WTREGEN` / Daily Treasury
Statement operating cash balance, since FRED's CSV endpoint is firewalled in this build)
against month-end **SPY** (yfinance, total-return adjusted). We split forward 1/2/3/6-month
SPY returns into months when the TGA is **drawing down** (liquidity injected) vs
**building** (reserves drained), compare each to the unconditional base rate, and add a
Welch *t*, a **Newey-West (HAC)** predictive regression, a placebo null, a lead/lag scan
and a tradable timing overlay. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| TGA tape | Treasury General Account operating cash balance ($B) — FRED `WTREGEN` / Daily Treasury Statement; **hardcoded monthly PROXY**, approximate levels |
| Equity tape | yfinance daily **SPY** adjusted close (total-return adjusted), month-end sampled |
| Window | 2005-01-31 → 2026-06-30 (**258** months; **21.4** years) |
| Signal | TGA change = balance vs **1 month** prior; **DRAWING DOWN** when change < 0 (injection = −change) |
| Entry / costs | **1-month execution lag** (act on the next month-end close); 10 bps one-way per switch on the overlay |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** FRED is firewalled here, and the true
> `WTREGEN` series is **weekly**; hardcoding ~1,000 weekly prints by hand would be false
> precision, so — following the desk convention for labelled proxies (Study 358
> watch-index, Study 708 eurovision-effect) — the TGA tape is an **approximate monthly
> end-of-month proxy** ($B). The landmark moves are faithful: the 2008 Supplementary
> Financing surge, the 2020 **COVID balloon toward ~$1.8T**, and the debt-ceiling
> drawdowns toward near-zero (2021, mid-**2023**, 2025). The exact monthly levels are
> approximate — the qualitative verdict (a noisy, near-zero, un-tradable link) is robust
> to the proxy, and finer **weekly** resolution is flagged as a Beat-7 extension.

## The signal — forward SPY returns when the TGA is DRAWING DOWN vs the base rate

1-month execution lag; the base column is *all* months. The believers say a DRAWDOWN
(liquidity injection) should *raise* the forward return; Welch *t* compares the
DRAWDOWN-set mean to the unconditional mean (a real lever ⇒ **significantly positive**).
The HAC *t* is the Newey-West slope of the forward return on the continuous injection.
The placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 random same-size month draws whose mean forward
return is **at least** the DRAWDOWN set's (i.e. as bullish or more).

| horizon | n drawdown | drawdown mean | build mean | base mean | draw up-rate | base up-rate | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month | 123 | **+0.91%** | +1.01% | +0.96% | 66% | 66% | **−0.11** | −0.44 | 0.564 |
| 2-month | 123 | **+2.13%** | +1.79% | +1.95% | 76% | 72% | **+0.27** | −0.06 | 0.379 |
| 3-month | 122 | **+3.58%** | +2.34% | +2.93% | 75% | 74% | **+0.85** | +0.79 | 0.163 |
| 6-month | 120 | **+6.07%** | +5.77% | +5.91% | 82% | 79% | **+0.13** | −0.37 | 0.448 |

Read it carefully. At the horizon the thesis cares about most — the **next month** — the
drawdown mean (**+0.91%**) sits *below* the base rate (**+0.96%**): the sign is the
**opposite** of the story. Only at 3 months does a mildly positive gap appear
(**+3.58% vs +2.93%**), and even there the Welch *t* is **+0.85** and the HAC *t* is
**+0.79** — nowhere near the *t* ≥ 2 bar. No horizon, and neither the split test nor the
HAC regression, produces a signal distinguishable from noise.

## The HAC (Newey-West) predictive regression — slope ≈ 0

Forward H-month SPY return regressed on the trailing liquidity injection (per +$100B
drawn down), Newey-West HAC lags = horizon to absorb the overlap.

| horizon | slope (per +$100B drawn) | HAC *t* | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month | **−0.11%** | −0.44 | 0.06% |
| 2-month | −0.03% | −0.06 | 0.00% |
| 3-month | +0.47% | +0.79 | 0.41% |
| 6-month | −0.29% | −0.37 | 0.07% |

The slope flips sign across horizons and explains essentially **zero** variance
(R² ≤ 0.4%). A +$100B drawdown moves the point estimate by a fraction of a percent with a
*t* that never leaves ±1. There is no dose-response of returns to the size of the
liquidity injection.

## The identification test — does the injection *lead* the market?

The pitch is that the injection comes **first**. We scan the correlation of the injection
at *t* against the SPY return over `[t+L, t+L+1]`. A genuine liquidity lever would show
its strongest *positive* correlation at a **positive** lead (injection first, market up
later).

| lead *L* (months) | −3 | −1 | 0 | +1 | +2 | +3 | +6 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr(injection, fwd SPY) | +0.08 | +0.05 | +0.09 | **−0.03** | +0.02 | +0.11 | −0.18 |

The structure is **incoherent noise**: the largest positive correlation sits at
**L = −5** (+0.13, the injection *lagging* the market) and the largest negative at
**L = +6** (−0.18). At exactly the positive leads a tradable lever needs — **L = +1, +2**
— the correlation is ≈ 0 (**−0.03**, +0.02). There is no coherent lead: the injection
neither cleanly leads nor lags, it just co-wanders. That is the core of the "hidden
liquidity lever? — Not supported" stamp.

## Tradability — the "hold when the TGA is drawing down" overlay

Hold SPY when the TGA is drawing down, sit in cash when it is building (one-month lag;
10 bps per switch, turnover one-way × NAV). Sharpe is excess-of-zero (the cash leg earns
0 here — a conservative, labelled simplification).

| book | ann. mean | ann. Sharpe | switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-and-hold SPY | **+11.6%** | **0.78** | — |
| overlay, gross | +7.4% | 0.72 | 147 |
| overlay, net @ 10 bps | **+6.7%** | **0.66** | 147 |

The overlay **underperforms buy-and-hold** on both return (**+6.7% vs +11.6%** net) and
Sharpe (**0.66 vs 0.78**) — even *gross*. Sitting in cash whenever the TGA builds forfeits
return (the TGA built through much of the 2016–2019 and 2023–2024 bull runs) without
buying enough downside protection to pay for it. Acting on the signal **loses money
relative to doing nothing.**

## Robustness — window, and the COVID dependence

| variation | n drawdown | drawdown 1m mean | base 1m mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| change **k = 1** (base) | 123 | +0.91% | +0.96% | **−0.11** | −0.44 |
| change **k = 2** | 113 | +0.92% | +0.96% | −0.09 | −0.02 |
| change **k = 3** | 104 | +1.58% | +0.96% | **+1.36** | +0.75 |
| **drop 2020–mid-2021** (ex-COVID) | 113 | +0.87% | +1.05% | −0.34 | +0.24 |

The strongest reading is a slow **k = 3** window (Welch *t* = +1.36) — still under the bar,
and a 3-month-old drawdown trend is a weaker version of the "immediate injection" the
thesis sells. Dropping the COVID balloon-and-drawdown (2020–mid-2021) leaves the 1-month
Welch *t* at **−0.34** — the wrong sign. No specification clears *t* = 2.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly TGA + SPY-like series with a *planted* link (a drawdown at *t*
lifts the capturable `[t+1, t+2]` forward return by `edge`). The detector + inference must
recover a planted edge and must **not** manufacture significance when the true edge is
zero.

| planted edge (monthly) | n drawdown | drawdown 1m mean | base 1m mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 128 | +0.74% | +0.54% | **+0.44** | +1.44 | 0.294 |
| **+0.04** (large link) | 128 | +4.85% | +2.64% | **+4.40** | +7.45 | 0.000 |

With **no** planted link the headline Welch test sits at *t* = +0.44 (placebo *p* = 0.29 —
no false positive); a large planted link drives Welch *t* to **+4.40** and HAC *t* to
**+7.45**. The machinery is unbiased and *does* bank a real drawdown→returns link when one
is present — so the real-tape null (Welch *t* ≈ 0, HAC *t* ≈ 0) is a *genuine* absence of
edge, not a broken test.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The thesis's own preferred horizon (next month) has the drawdown mean
  *below* base (**+0.91% vs +0.96%** — wrong sign); across 1/2/3/6 months the Welch *t*
  peaks at **+0.85** and the HAC slope explains ≤ 0.4% of variance with a *t* that never
  leaves ±1. Indistinguishable from noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "hold when drawing down" overlay **underperforms
  buy-and-hold** gross *and* net (**+6.7% vs +11.6%**, Sharpe **0.66 vs 0.78**). Acting on
  the signal *destroys* return. Nothing to allocate to.
- **Hidden liquidity lever? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The lead/lag scan is incoherent — near-zero
  (**−0.03 / +0.02**) at exactly the positive leads a real lever needs, with its extremes
  scattered at *L* = −5 and *L* = +6. The injection neither leads nor lags cleanly; it
  co-wanders with a shared macro backdrop. The mechanism the story rests on doesn't show
  up in the tape.
